newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Herald poll confirms Labour closing on National.
newsitem.headline: NZ Herald poll confirms Labour closing on National.

text.p: An opinion poll in the New Zealand Herald newspaper on the eve of Saturday's general election provided further evidence that the opposition Labour Party is closing on the conservative National Party government.
The poll showed National falling one point to 33 percent in the past week, with Labour gaining 1.7 to 29.4 percent.
Economic nationalist New Zealand First rose two to 16, while the left-wing Alliance slipped two to 10.6 percent.

The radical free-market Act New Zealand party was up 1.9 points to 6.5 percent. Parties need to win five percent of the vote or more to get MPs into parliament unless they succeed in winning one of the 65 constituency seats.
The Christian Coalition fell 0.6 points to 3.4 percent and looks increasingly unlikely to win seats. Both Act and the Christians are seen as potential coalition partners for National.

The poll would give National 41 seats, Labour 37, New Zealand First 20, the Alliance 13, Act eight and the centrist United Party one in the new parliament. United is expected to win a Wellington constituency seat.
The poll confirmed Labour, New Zealand First and the Alliance appear jointly set to win a clear majority of seats and could oust National if they can agree on a programme to govern.
